# Windows worker identity query

Arcane uses a fixed read-only native helper for its own asset-worker identity checks. The helper accepts no arguments and reads only the validated decimal ARCANE_WORKER_PID environment variable. It opens that exact PID once with query/synchronize rights, checks liveness before and after reading creation FILETIME and executable path through the same handle, closes the handle and emits one bounded UTF-8 JSON result. Access denial, malformed input or metadata/close failure cannot prove absence. It never enumerates or terminates processes, changes privileges or reads provider credentials.

The production host verifies the reviewed source, executable and receipt before selecting the helper. Missing, altered, redirected or hard-linked payloads are unavailable; the production host does not silently choose PowerShell instead. The five-second query deadline, seven-second lost-callback watchdog, 4096-byte output cap, exact creation-time comparison and unknown-ownership fences remain unchanged. The legacy constant PowerShell invocation remains a custom-host compatibility/test path, not the default packaged Windows path.

The executable is first-party build output. It is included in the release integrity closure with workers/windows/WorkerIdentity.cs and apps/desktop/host-tools/worker-query/manifest.json. Source SHA-256 uses UTF-8 with CRLF normalized to LF so Git checkout line endings do not change source identity. Executable bytes and receipt fields remain exact. SSH-signed source commits and closed release hashes do not imply Windows Authenticode signing.

To rebuild deliberately on Windows, use node scripts/build-worker-query.mjs. It uses the fixed system .NET compiler, no downloaded compiler or shell. The system compiler's normal Windows-servicing hard links are accepted; generated files remain direct single-link files. Review the changed C# source and resulting binary, then update the reviewed pins in both scripts/managed-worker-query.mjs and packages/asset-pipeline/src/worker-identity.ts. A rebuild is not an automatic pin update and is not part of customer startup. Run strict compilation, worker identity/custody/recovery tests, native Windows Unicode/exit tests and release integrity tests before publishing a new helper.
